archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing-and-accuracy)
archetype.definition: Prescott wins from the pocket on rhythm and placement. He gets the ball out in under three seconds to a short-to-intermediate tree and leans on one dominant target rather than his legs or the deep ball.

report.headline: Efficient, accurate and Lamb-driven; the shootout script is doing some of the lifting.
report.take:
Four games in, Prescott is playing like his best seasons. He is sixth in EPA per dropback (0.312) and sixth in CPOE (6.3), which looks like 2023 (third in EPA/play) and a step up from a solid 2025 (12th). The method hasn't changed. His 2.73-second time to throw sits right on his career band, his intended air yards are a modest 7.5, and he throws a bit short of the sticks on average. His bad-throw rate of 11.3% matches his 2023 and 2025 lows. Nothing about how he plays is new. What's new is how well it is converting.

Two things drive the season. The first is CeeDee Lamb: 47 targets, nearly a third of Prescott's attempts, at 0.886 EPA per target, more than double anyone else on the roster. The second is the middle of the field between 10 and 19 yards, where Prescott is at 0.733 EPA with four touchdowns on 32 throws. The red zone has been unusually kind: seven of his eight touchdowns came there on 23 attempts. Underneath it all is a team context that forces him to throw. Dallas ranks 31st in defensive EPA and dead last against the pass. The Cowboys have allowed 20 or more points every week, and all four games went over the total. He has thrown 40 and 45 times in the last two games because he had to.

The numbers hide a few things. His 7.1 yards per attempt ranks only 22nd, dragged down by 32 throws behind the line at -0.352 EPA, a screen-heavy diet that wastes about a fifth of his attempts. Split by game state, he is very good rather than great where it counts: 0.15 EPA on the 126 plays within one score. The gaudy figures come from the 24 snaps trailing by nine or more. The ball-security numbers will also move. One interception in 150 attempts and an 11.5% pressure-to-sack rate are both well below anything in his career; he has thrown 9-15 picks in every full recent season.

Where it's heading: the core holds, with accuracy, quick processing and Lamb all repeatable. Touchdown efficiency and interception luck should drift toward his normal. Volume will keep tracking a defense that can't get off the field, and this week tests that from the other side, as a heavy favorite against a backup quarterback.

strengths.title: Rhythm accuracy in the intermediate middle
strengths.body: Prescott is completing passes well above expectation, and the value concentrates at 10-19 yards and between the numbers. That is timing-and-placement work, not scramble-drill luck. His career CPOE has mostly been positive, so the skill is real, though a 6+ figure is at the top of his range and likely settles a bit.

strengths.title: Lamb as the engine
strengths.body: Lamb draws 47 targets at 0.886 EPA each, which is the single biggest reason Dallas ranks third in pass EPA. Concentrating on the best receiver is sound and sustainable. It does make the offense brittle if a defense can bracket him, because the next-best options fall off quickly.

strengths.title: Clean decisions under fire
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate matches the 2023 and 2025 seasons, his two cleanest years, so the decision-making is a trait and not a blip. He has converted half his third downs at 6.3 yards to go, completing passes 11.4 points over expectation there.

concerns.title: Screen-heavy diet caps yards per attempt
concerns.body: Thirty-two throws behind the line have produced negative EPA. That is why a top-six EPA passer ranks 22nd in yards per attempt. This is a scheme choice, not a Prescott flaw, but it means his efficiency rests heavily on the downfield throws continuing to hit.

concerns.title: Turnover and sack luck will fade
concerns.body: A 0.7% interception rate and an 11.5% pressure-to-sack rate are both far below his history. He threw 10 picks in 2025, and his pressure-to-sack rate ran 24-35% in recent seasons. Expect more giveaways and more sacks on the same quality of play.

concerns.title: Red-zone TD rate is running hot
concerns.body: Seven touchdowns on 23 red-zone attempts, while completing only 56.5% of them, is a rate that rarely holds. His touchdown total is more likely to cool than his yardage.

trend.note: His per-dropback efficiency has stayed positive every week, peaking against Washington and easing slightly in Houston. Volume has climbed to 40 and 45 attempts as close games demanded it. His air yards have shortened each week, from 8.3 to 6.7 intended, so the yardage rise is a volume story, not a downfield one.

nextGame.headline: Thin Bucs secondary, weak pass rush, but a lopsided script caps volume.
nextGame.body:
Tampa Bay's defense ranks fifth in EPA, but the strength is up front against the run (third). Against the pass it is 14th, and it rarely hits or sacks the quarterback. That suits a rhythm thrower whose sack numbers are already low. Tampa does limit explosive passes, ranking ninth, so this sets up as Prescott's underneath-and-intermediate game rather than a deep one. A top run defense against a Dallas run game that is already below average should keep the ball in his hands on early downs.

Availability tilts toward Dallas. Tampa is without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (97% of snaps, out 2-4 weeks with a rib fracture) and corner Benjamin Morrison, and linebacker Josiah Trotter is limited. That is a lot of coverage missing over the middle, exactly where Prescott is doing damage. The bigger effect may be indirect: Baker Mayfield is out, and an offense already 31st in pass EPA now plays a backup on a four-day turnaround. On Dallas's side, guard Tyler Smith is on IR but practicing in a limited role; the line has been fine without him, so a return would be a bonus. The spread implies a Dallas lead, which trims Prescott's attempts in the second half.

keyMatchups.title: Middle of field without Winfield
keyMatchups.body: Prescott has four touchdowns and 0.512 EPA on throws to the middle. Tampa loses its every-down safety, plus a corner and possibly a linebacker. Lamb working the seams against a reshuffled back end is the main edge here.

keyMatchups.title: Little pressure from the Bucs
keyMatchups.body: Tampa ranks near the bottom in hitting and sacking the quarterback. Prescott is already one of the hardest quarterbacks to sack. Expect a clean pocket, which supports his accuracy but removes the scramble yards that pressure sometimes produces.

keyMatchups.title: Game script versus a backup QB
keyMatchups.body: Tampa's offense was 31st in pass EPA even before losing Mayfield. If Dallas leads early, the passing volume behind his recent 40-plus-attempt games disappears. Dallas's porous defense is the one thing that could keep him throwing.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dallas keeps throwing with a lead. If it keeps passing against Tampa's top-three run defense, Prescott's volume survives the script.

restOfSeason.body:
The skill side looks durable. His accuracy, quick decisions and low bad-throw rate match his best seasons, and Lamb's usage is structural. A defense this bad keeps Dallas in high-scoring games and keeps Prescott's attempts high, which supports the yardage.

What regresses is the margin stuff. The interception rate should roughly double toward his normal, the sack rate should creep up, and the red-zone touchdown rate should cool. Expect a top-10 to top-12 efficiency passer with strong volume, closer to 2025 than to a career year.

bets.reason: Dallas has won by double digits once in four games, and its defense ranks 31st in EPA and last against the pass, so it lets opponents hang around. Tampa's defense ranks fifth, which limits how far Dallas can pull away even against a backup QB.

Tampa allows 227 passing yards a game to quarterbacks and ranks ninth in limiting explosive passes. Prescott's recent yardage came on 40-45 attempts in close games, a volume a 9.5-point favorite is unlikely to need.
Seven of his eight touchdowns came on 23 red-zone attempts, a rate that should cool. Tampa allows 1.5 passing touchdowns a game to the position.

confidence.note: Four-game sample consistent with his career, but next game's script is uncertain.
